notes: Summary: Mid-market B2B productivity SaaS (workflow automation). Evaluating embeddings + semantic search to power in-app contextual search and recommendation surfaces.
Business drivers: Improve search relevance for user knowledge bases, reduce reliance on keyword + boolean fallbacks, enable fast similarity-based recommendations across 500k+ indexed docs.

Workloads: monthly batch embed pipeline (approx 1M docs/month initially), nightly re-index, nearline query traffic for active customers (p95 queries per second ~ 30-50), occasional high-throughput bulk similarity jobs for analytics.

Performance targets: top-k query latency target <50ms (tail goal <100ms), embed generation throughput target for batch jobs >10k embeds/min for POC, cost-sensitive for token pricing and batch compute.
Current stack: planning to integrate Redwood Hosted API for POC embeddings, will route vectors into Pinecone for vector DB; exploring Dedicated later for predictable throughput and lower unit costs.
Security: must pass SOC2 audit, require SSO/SAML for console access, audit logs + KMS key support for at-rest encryption; EU customers require regional residency option.
Quote from Lena: "We need embeddings that scale with predictable cost — if the math works, Dedicated makes sense."

POC scope: 1) hosted embeddings for 100k-doc sample and search test; 2) measure embed latency and throughput; 3) validate vector DB end-to-end (Pinecone + fallback to Weaviate); 4) run nightly batch with Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization.
Cost sensitivity: internal model shows $/embed must be < $0.00045 for target ARR margins; will push on pricing for committed dedicated pools.

Integration notes: engineering prefers REST SDK, needs streaming progress for long batch jobs, asks for guidance on tokenization/embedding model selection and recommended quantization profiles for Dedicated.
Open items: Dedicated pricing worksheet, SLA for vector DB integration (indexing latency), confirm whether Redwood can provide sample throughput benchmarks with our doc size distribution.
